title: How to recognise a Simca P60: what the front end and line change in 1959
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: The P60 does not begin from a wholly new shell, yet its nose, roofline and interior are enough to push the Aronde into another era of style.
content:
The P60 often intrigues because it looks both like a prolonged Aronde and like a new car. To read it properly, one has to look at what Simca changes precisely for the 1959 model year.

A much more assertive front end

The grille opens more widely and the nose looks more deliberate than on the Aronde 1300 with Oceane line. The car clearly wants to enter a new decade without fully denying its base.

That evolution is often enough to date the spirit of the car. The P60 wants to draw attention more openly than the previous Aronde.

A roof and rear that alter the balance

The profile matters just as much. Roofline, rear window and general treatment of the body shift the model’s balance toward something more modern, and sometimes more heavily styled too.

This is where one best sees the Simca logic: push an older success far enough to give it further commercial life.

A true P60 takes more than one clue to identify

As with many popular 1950s cars, mixed parts are common. The nose, cabin, trim, claimed version and overall coherence all need to be read together.

Good identification does not rest on one sign alone. It depends on replacing the car inside the last great phase of Aronde history.

This note extends the page the Simca P60. Within the same cluster, the next useful step is P60 Etoile, Elysee, Monthlery and Monaco: what differences really matter.
